question: When does Nosrat recommend salting a chicken you plan to roast?
options: A day ahead, if you can
answer: Ideally a day ahead, or at least a few hours. Given time, salt dissolves and spreads through the meat, seasoning it evenly and helping its proteins hold on to moisture, so it comes out juicier. Nosrat's rule: salt meat early, rather than relying on salt sprinkled at the end.
move: Seasoning works with time; salt early and let it spread.
trap: 'Just before serving': salt seems to dry meat out.
simply: Salt a chicken the night before, and the salt has time to soak in, so the meat tastes seasoned all through and stays juicier.
why: One change in timing makes a big difference. In cooking, as elsewhere, when you do something can matter as much as what you do.
